chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The shroud is not perfumed with incense.

key_terms.يُجَمَّرُ: Is perfumed with incense (burning musk or similar substances)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on perfuming the shroud with incense in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the prohibition of burning incense directly on the shroud, reflecting the Shia emphasis on simplicity and avoiding the ostentatious embellishment of the deceased. It is often discussed alongside the related ruling of warming the water for washing, highlighting a consistent theme of practicality and modesty in funeral rites. The ruling underscores the distinction between honoring the dead and engaging in excessive ritualistic display.
